newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-BA talks tough despite strike damage.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-BA talks tough despite strike damage.

text.p: British Airways on Wednesday refused to buckle under the pressure of a cabin crew strike which grounded half its flights out of London, branding the strike illegal and saying it was considering taking the union to court.
British Airways said it would not negotiate the terms of a deal to cut costs by 42 million pounds ($71 million), which provoked the dispute by the Transport and General Workers Union (T&G).
"We have written to the T&G and demanded to know what they intend to do about this illegal action," said Mike Street, BA's director of operations.
"We have given them a deadline of 3 pm (1400 GMT) this afternoon."

BA said it would review its position if the union had not responded by the deadline but hinted that it could seek legal redress, including compensation from the union for losses incurred. It says there were discrepancies in the strike ballot.
BA declined to specify the losses it was facing as a result of the strike.
There was no-one from the T&G immediately available to comment on BA's threat of legal action, but officials said earlier that the strike had strong backing.
"Despite all the threats, I can report that the dispute is solid," T&G General Secretary Bill Morris told the union's conference in Brighton.
The cabin crew strike began at 0500 GMT on Wednesday, forcing the airline to cancel between 20 and 30 percent of the 1,000 flights it operates worldwide each day.
Pickets carrying banners gathered in the early morning sun near BA's headquarters at Heathrow, while usually frenetic Terminal One was eerily quiet.
Pickets were also stationed outside other British airports and some were even flown to New York to try to win support from workers there.
British Airways said a number of union members had reported to work as normal and more than thousand more had called in sick, rather than strike, because of fears of crossing a picket line.
"It is clear to us now that the strike is not well supported," said Kevin Murray, BA director of communications. "A large number of crew are coming into work."
The company said that by 1400 GMT, 113 cabin crew had reported for work with only 101 officially declaring themselves on strike. Between 1,400 and 1,500 had reported sick.

Asked whether the crew had reported sick rather than go on strike because of BA's threats that strikers would lose perks and face a lockout, Walker said: "Crew have not been threatened. We have not intimidated and never would intimidate any of our employees."
BA said the T&G had already accepted the necessity of the 42 million pounds cost cuts.
"The only way to achieve that target is through the deal on the table," Mervyn Walker, director of human resources told a newsconference.
"We will not discuss the terms of the deal."

The airline said it hoped to operate a wider schedule of flights on Thursday and Friday, but haven't yet specified what services they will be able to run. ba quotes. British airways refusing to negotiate and threatening legal action unless union gives way by 3pm. ($ = 0.592 British Pounds)
